text:
dmitri: Hey — seeing a sudden spike in Kibana query latency and a ton of SLO alerts for the GPU fleet central-log search around 13:04 UTC. Queries that normally return <200ms are timing out. Anyone else seeing this?

maya: I saw the alerts too. grafana shows indexer CPU and write latency for log-shards-eu-west1 up ~3x.

ops-bot: [ALERT] central-log-search-slo:latency (page) fired for `team:eng-sre` (threshold breached 2m)

sam: Are we sure it's Kibana and not Loki ingest backpressure? Last time indexer CPU spiked we had a burst of high-cardinality logs from a canary rollout.

anita: good call — pulling recent logs. Running a focused Loki query to check ingestion rate.

anita: Loki query I'm running:```
{job="central-logs", cluster="eu-west1"} | json | __error__!="" | count_over_time(1m)
```

maya: Also paging query sampling config: looks like `query_sampling: 100%` for the dashboard, but I remember we enabled rate-limited sampling on the gateway last week. Might be mismatch.

dmitri: I think the issue is query amplification from dashboard panels. A recent dashboard change may now be issuing long time-range queries every 30s. Those are hammering the indexers.

sam: For faster triage: can we temporarily reduce dashboard refresh to 1m and drop time window to 1h? Also start a short-term rate-limit on kibana-proxy for heavy queries.

anita: Applying proxy throttle for `kibana/*` endpoints now (10r/s) — monitoring.

ops-bot: [ACTION] Throttle applied to kibana-proxy for service `central-logs` by anita (manual)

maya: After throttle, cluster CPU down to 1.6x baseline and Kibana query p95 is improving. But still seeing a lot of high-cardinality traces where correlation IDs are missing — makes join-based troubleshooting hard.

dmitri: We should run a quick join check between trace IDs in the ingest pipeline and logs to see if trace propagation dropped at the proxy. Query I used to find missing trace ids:```
{app="log-forwarder"} | json | !trace_id | count_over_time(5m)
```

anita: Results show a small spike of logs without trace_id coinciding with the canary rollout timestamp. Looks like the rollout added a new log library that overwrote the trace header.

sam: If that's true, we need to roll back that canary or patch the library quickly. Is it the k8s deployment `frontend-canary`?

anita: Yes — deployment `frontend-canary` had a change in `logger` dependency. I opened a rollback PR and started rollback at 13:12 UTC.

maya: Good. For longer-term: add an SLO for correlation completeness (trace_id present) and an alert when it drops >0.5% for 5m. Also add sampling tags to Kibana queries so heavy dashboards can be safely sampled.

dmitri: Agreed. Also we should adjust alert runbook to differentiate query-latency-caused-by-backend (indexer CPU) vs client-heavy-dashboard. Right now alert noise is too high.

sam: Quick checklist for postmortem:
- rollback confirmed ✅
- throttle applied ✅
- PR to fix logger dep open: https://git.company/repo/pull/987
- create SLO & alert for correlation completeness (SRE task)
- update kibana dashboards with sampling hints (product/observability)

anita: Rollback finished at 13:16 UTC — correlation rates returning to normal. I'll leave throttle for 10 min then remove if stable.

ops-bot: [RESOLVE] central-log-search-slo:latency resolved (no longer firing)

maya: Folks, can someone add a short note to the central-logs runbook about dashboard time-range defaults and a command to quickly throttle kibana-proxy? Saves people fiddling during noise.

dmitri: I'll add it and create the SLO ticket. Labels: `infra-observability`, `postmortem-needed`

sam: Thx all — nice fast triage. I think we avoided a larger incident by throttling and rollback.

anita: leaving logs + queries used in #runbooks/central-logs gist: https://internal.gist/abcd1234 — contains the loki/kibana queries and proxy commands we ran.

maya: follow-up items assigned. I'll put a short postmortem note in #postmortems if nobody beats me to it. :thumbsup:

dmitri: closing thread, will ping when runbook PR is up."
